title: Harvey on the We're Here
text:
Harvey Cheyne was fifteen, the spoiled son of an American railroad millionaire, and he was insufferable to everyone on the ocean liner taking him to Europe. One day, seasick, he fell overboard off the Grand Banks of Newfoundland. A Portuguese fisherman named Manuel picked him out of the sea and brought him aboard the fishing schooner We're Here, from Gloucester, Massachusetts.

Harvey demanded that the captain, Disko Troop, take him straight to New York, promising his father would pay. Troop did not believe a word about the millionaire father and would not cut short the fishing season. When Harvey accused him of stealing the money he had lost overboard, Troop knocked him down. Then he offered Harvey a job as a ship's boy for ten dollars and a half a month.

With nothing else to do, Harvey took it. Dan, the captain's son, became his friend. Harvey learned to bait hooks, row a dory, clean and salt the cod, keep watch and take his share of every job, and the crew began to treat him as one of them. For the first time in his life he was valued for what he did.

At the end of the season the We're Here sailed home to Gloucester, and Harvey's parents came to fetch him. They found a different boy.
lesson: Respect in a team is earned by doing your share of the real work. Being needed by others can change a person more than any amount of comfort.
people: Harvey Cheyne, Disko Troop, Dan Troop, Manuel
location: England and the United States (novel set on the Grand Banks and in Gloucester, Massachusetts)
